findings.title: Substring match upsamples negated and compound `event.type:error` queries
findings.description: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True when `"event.type:error" in query`. That is a substring test, so `!event.type:error` matches. With the default `discover` dataset, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` then returns True and `count()` becomes `upsampled_count() as count`, which sums `sample_weight` over rows the query was meant to exclude. The docstring at lines 105-107 says upsampling applies only to error events, so this contradicts the stated intent. The existing test (`tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py#test_is_error_focused_query`) only covers the exact strings `event.type:error` and `event.type:transaction`, so it misses this. Parse the query tokens, or match the condition exactly, and add a `!event.type:error` case.

findings.title: `transformAliasToInputFormat=1` silently zeroes the upsampled series
findings.description: The transform emits the alias `count`. The builder's result remapping (`search/events/builder/base.py:1566-1580`, applied to data rows at `:1613-1616`) rewrites that key to `function_alias_map[...].field`, which is the raw string `upsampled_count() as count`. When `transformAliasToInputFormat=1` is set (`organization_events_stats.py:205-207`), `resolve_axis_column` returns the original `count()` as the lookup key (`api/bases/organization_events.py:75-76`). `serializers/snuba.py:92` then does `r.get(column, 0)`, so every bucket comes back as `0` with no error. This affects allowlisted discover/errors queries that send the flag. The frontend sends this flag from 15 files under `static/app`, though the ones I checked are span datasets, so I have not confirmed that discover callers send it. Fix the key mismatch, and add an endpoint test that sends `transformAliasToInputFormat=1`.

findings.title: Eligibility uses the outer dataset and raw request query, not what actually runs
findings.description: `_get_event_stats` passes `dataset` (the outer variable from line 170) and `request.GET["query"]` to the helper. The queries that actually run use `scoped_dataset`, `split_dataset`, and the rewritten `query` (lines 364, 383, 426). The split path (line 344) only runs when the outer dataset is a metrics dataset, and `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns False for those, so split-path queries are never upsampled while the non-split path is. Two widgets with the same query can therefore use different count semantics. Pass the dataset and query that are actually executed.

findings.title: Only the literal `count()` is rewritten
findings.description: The check is `column_lower == "count()"`, an exact match. Equations pass through the same `query_columns` list (`api/bases/organization_events.py:71` handles `is_equation`), so `equation|count() * 2` stays unweighted while plain `count()` on the same chart is upsampled. Aliased forms such as `count() as x` also skip the rewrite. The top-N selection query (`snuba/discover.py:489-505`) ranks by the request `orderby` over raw rows, while the series values are weighted. The docstring's "aggregation functions" overstates the coverage. Decide the scope explicitly and document it.

findings.title: Eligibility cache has no invalidation and an unmeasured justification
findings.description: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` has no callers in the repo (grep confirmed). Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds (line 38), so an allowlist change takes up to a minute to apply, and nothing invalidates the entry even though the docstring says it should be called on change. The performance rationale (lines 23-25) is not backed by anything in the diff. Either wire the invalidation into the option-change path or drop the cache. Separately, the key uses builtin `hash()` on a tuple (lines 27 and 73); a 64-bit collision would return another project set's eligibility, and a sorted string key avoids that.

findings.title: `upsampled_count` is publicly callable
findings.description: The new function is registered without `private=True`, unlike the internal helper `column_hash` directly above it (line 1039). `is_accessible` (`search/events/fields.py:569`) gates private functions behind `functions_acl`, so this change makes the function callable by any API user on any project, including non-allowlisted projects where the comment says `sample_weight` is not guaranteed. Also, `toInt64` returns an integer, so `default_result_type="integer"` would be more accurate than `"number"`.

findings.title: Duplicated transform call sites and redundant variables
findings.description: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` is called at three sites (lines 233, 277, and 296), and the initial `final_columns = query_columns` is overwritten on every path. `upsampling_enabled = should_upsample` is a pointless alias. Compute once before branching, for example `final_columns = transform(...) if should_upsample else query_columns`, so a future branch cannot miss the transform.

findings.title: Test coverage misses the defects above, and the tests were not run
findings.description: Missing cases: `!event.type:error` (would have caught the first FAIL), `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, `transformAliasToInputFormat=1` through the endpoint (second FAIL), the `topEvents` branch of `_get_event_stats` (`organization_events_stats.py:229-272`), the cache hit and miss paths in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, and direct resolution of `upsampled_count`. The endpoint test also depends on Snuba computing `sample_weight` from the factory's `sample_rate`, which I could not confirm here. I have not run any of these tests.

findings.title: Test factory swallows exceptions
findings.description: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` has two bare `except Exception: pass` blocks. The only failure the first one can hit is `contexts` being `None` or a non-dict, which should be a `None` guard (`normalized_data.get("contexts") or {}`), not a swallowed exception. The helper also runs for every event that `store_event` creates. Keep this logic in the test class, or make it explicit rather than silent.

findings.title: Unrelated `topEvents` message change
findings.description: The message changes from "If topEvents needs to be at least 1" to "topEvents needs to be at least 1". This matches `organization_events_timeseries.py:134`, so it is a valid consistency fix, but it has nothing to do with upsampling. It is a public API string change, so clients that match on it will break. No test pins the old text. Ship it in a separate commit.

findings.title: Trailing whitespace on blank lines
findings.description: Seven lines in `error_upsampling.py` contain trailing whitespace, and three in `organization_events_stats.py` (lines 223, 234, and 278). Run the formatter; ruff format normally strips these.

findings.title: Comments contradict the code
findings.description: The `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` docstring says it reads configuration fresh on every call, "intentional", while the caller caches that result for 60 seconds (lines 27-38). The endpoint comments at `organization_events_stats.py:218-219`, `224-225`, and `230-231` call the check an "early" "performance optimization" and claim a "late transformation ensures we use the most current schema assumptions". None of that is what the code does.

findings.title: Loose type on the dataset parameter
findings.description: `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset: Any, ...)` should use `ModuleType`, as its sibling `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` does at line 16.

findings.title: Test setup reassigns the logged-in user
findings.description: `self.login_as(user=self.user)` runs at line 3559, then `self.user` is reassigned at line 3566. The requests therefore run as the original user, while the event tags reference the new one. `self.authed_user` (line 3560) is never used. Rename the variables so the setup reads clearly.

findings.title: Direct `Organization.objects.create` in the unit test
findings.description: This is the only direct `Organization.objects.create` under `tests/sentry/api`. The neighboring tests use the `self.create_organization()` fixture, so this should follow the same convention.
